Straight answers before you commit.

How we pick the robot, pay for it, get it running, and keep it running — plain answers, no pitch. Don't see your question? Tell us the job and we'll answer it directly.

Common questions

What does it cost to put a robot to work?
Depends on the robot, the job, and the site — we quote every deployment before you commit. As a reference point, buying a robot outright typically runs $4,000–$50,000, plus upkeep. Buy it, lease it, or rent it monthly — your CFO picks the structure, and we surface the options at the start, not after you have fallen for a machine.
What is included when Service Robot Co. runs a deployment?
Six things, one partner: we design the fit with a free site assessment, integrate the robot with the systems you already run, deploy it on a timeline that does not stop your operation, finance it however works for you, train your team until it is routine, and service it for life. You get a working robot on site — not four vendors to manage.
Should I buy, lease, or rent?
Whichever keeps your cash where you want it. Buying makes sense when you are certain about the job long-term. Leasing or renting monthly keeps the cost predictable and the downtime risk on us. We lay out all three before you decide.
How does deployment actually work?
We start with a free site assessment — we walk your space, learn the job, and tell you which robot fits, or that none does yet. Then we install on a phased timeline that does not stop your operation, connect the robot to the systems you already use, and train your team on their shift until running it feels routine.
What happens if the robot breaks down?
You call one number. 10-minute remote triage during business hours, 24-hour nationwide on-site dispatch, 24/7 emergency response. One in three issues never need a truck. A broken robot is our problem, not your downtime.
Do you build your own robots?
No — we are an integrator, not an OEM. We deploy and service robots from category-leading manufacturers across cleaning, delivery, AMR, cobot, and more. The OEM builds the machine; we own getting it working on your floor and keeping it that way.
Which robot do I need for my job?
Tell us the work and we will match it. Warehouses and distribution centers usually need AMRs and material handling robots; hospitals and hotels want delivery and cleaning robots; manufacturers want cobots and industrial arms. See every robot by type, or find your operation on Industries — either way, we match the robot to the job and quote it.
What if nothing fits my site yet?
We will tell you. The site assessment is free, and if no robot fits your operation today, we say so — you do not pay to find out.
